subject: Atlas Dynamics — capacity hedging & GPU fitment RFI
messages:
From: Atlas Dynamics <procurement@atlasdynamics.com>
To: jordan_blake@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: RFI: Dedicated capacity hedging and GPU fitment

Hi Jordan,

Thanks for the introductory call yesterday. As we prepare the internal procurement packet, we need a concise RFI focused on two topics: (1) hedging / runway options for capacity commitments (phased commitments, burst buffers, early renewal credits), and (2) recommended GPU families and mix for a mixed workload (short chat inference + medium-length summarization + embedding bulk jobs).

Could you provide a short questionnaire-style response and any quantitative models you use to map throughput to GPU counts? We're targeting a 12–18 month runway with predictable unit economics. Attachments we can accept: CSV or XLSX for cost/runway worksheets.

Appreciate a reply by end of next week.

Best,
Sandeep Rao
Head of Platform Procurement
Atlas Dynamics

[Attachment: atlas_rfi_v1.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: jordan_blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Atlas Dynamics <procurement@atlasdynamics.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-01T10:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RFI: Dedicated capacity hedging and GPU fitment

Sandeep —

Thanks for the clear ask. Attached is a concise RFI response and a modeling workbook: atlas_rfi_answers.xlsx and gpu_runway_model.csv. Highlights up front:

- Hedging options: phased commitments (3/6/12 month tranches), refundable burst credits, and early-renewal credit stacks. We provide decision rules for shifting burst buffer to committed lanes if utilization stays > 70% for two consecutive billing cycles.
- GPU mix recommendation: for your mixed profile we typically propose a blended pool: 30% A100-80GB (high-throughput for bulk embeddings), 50% A800/RTX7000-equivalent (balanced latency and cost for chat), 20% H100-like nodes (low-latency tail-sensitive SLOs). We provide quantized variants for cost reduction on embedding pipelines.
- Throughput mapping: the workbook includes per-model tokens/sec extrapolations and a conservative 15% safety margin.

Next steps: review the workbook, tell us which commit cadence you'd prefer, and we can produce a 1-page SLA/concession table for procurement.

Regards,
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Accounts — Redwood Inference

[Attachments: atlas_rfi_answers.xlsx, gpu_runway_model.csv]

From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: jordan_blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-02T08:23:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RFI: Dedicated capacity hedging and GPU fitment

Jordan / Kim —

Quick internal notes on model assumptions I used for the workbook:

- Assumed 80M token/day for embedding pipeline (batched), embedding model throughput 3500 tokens/sec on A100-80GB quantized path.
- Chat workload: 2000 qps peak, 95th perc latency target < 200ms; used A800-equivalent for steady-state with H100 for 5% of slots to handle spike tail.
- Burst policy: allow 25% burst capacity up to 30 days per quarter, convert to committed if consumed > 60% across 2 months.

I've flagged two cells in gpu_runway_model.csv that change recommendations if embedding batch sizes are < 512 or > 4096 — want to confirm Atlas' batch profile.

-Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer

[Inline: quoted cells referenced]

From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: jordan_blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-02T11:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RFI: Dedicated capacity hedging and GPU fitment

Ben —

Thanks. A couple of procurement-oriented bullets to include before we send to Atlas:

- Pricing floors for long-term commits (12+ months) with CPI-linked annual adjustments (cap 3%).
- A 'convert-to-commit' clause: consumed burst credits that exceed threshold convert at a discounted amortized rate but with a 90-day notice window.
- Data handling: confirm the Private deployment option for logs retention > 12 months (customer asked about audit log retention).

I'll draft the concession table; Jordan, can you confirm region (us-west) and whether Atlas needs on-prem options?

-Kim
Director, Enterprise Sales Ops

From: Sandeep Rao <sandeep@atlasdynamics.com>
To: jordan_blake@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@atlasdynamics.com
Date: 2026-10-04T09:55:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RFI: Dedicated capacity hedging and GPU fitment

Jordan / Team —

Thanks for the fast turnaround and workbook. A few clarifying answers:

- Batch distribution for embeddings: generally 1024 tokens per batch, nightly windows with bursts during ETL runs.
- Region: us-west primary, eu-west for disaster recovery (DR) copy — we'll want geo-fallback policies.
- On-prem: not needed at initial phase. We will, however, require 18-month retention of audit logs (SOC2 scope).

Can you update the workbook to reflect 1024 batch size and provide two commit cadence options (6+12 mix and straight 12-month commit) with our estimated ingest profile? Also please include the procurement concession table Kim noted.

Looking forward to the updated file.

Best,
Sandeep

From: jordan_blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Atlas Dynamics <procurement@atlasdynamics.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai, dev_patel@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-05T16:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RFI: Dedicated capacity hedging and GPU fitment

Sandeep —

Appreciate the clarifications. Attached is an updated workbook and a 1-page concession table (commitment-hedge-options.pdf) that covers:

- Two cadence scenarios: (A) 6-month pilot + convert to 12-month at month 7 with a step-down credit schedule, (B) immediate 12-month commit with larger upfront discount and capped CPI adjustment.
- Runway numbers updated for 1024 batch embedding size and us-west primary / eu-west DR. You'll see the embedding GPU count drops ~4% vs conservative 512 case due to improved batch efficiency.
- Audit log retention: Private control-plane option toggles 18-month retention; we include KMS integration notes in the Drive link.

Next steps: we can set a 30-min procurement walkthrough Thursday or Friday — propose Thu 10/07 10:00am PT. If that works, I'll send an invite and a short agenda (workbook walkthrough + concession Q&A + legal handoff).

Thanks,
Jordan
Enterprise Accounts — Redwood Inference

[Attachments: commitment-hedge-options.pdf, updated_gpu_runway_model.csv]
